name: Kumyk

ancestors.notes: Descent from Proto-Turkic (Kipchak branch, Kipchak-Cuman group).
Russian adstrate: Soviet-era lexicon and long Dagestan/Caucasus regional contact.
Arabic adstrate: religious/scholarly vocabulary via the Islamic literary tradition.

notes: Kumyk (къумукъ тил), a Kipchak Turkic language of Dagestan, Russia, written in a Cyrillic alphabet reformed in 1938: the Russian letters plus the digraphs ⟨гъ⟩ /ʁ/, ⟨гь⟩ /h/, ⟨къ⟩ /q/, ⟨нг⟩ /ŋ/ (borrowed from the Caucasian-contact convention shared with Karachay-Balkar/Nogai) and the umlaut letters ⟨оь⟩ /ø/, ⟨уь⟩ /y/. ⟨къ⟩ /q/ alternates with a voiced [ɢ] allophone in complementary distribution, listed as an allophone rather than a separate grapheme. Vowel harmony (front/back, rounding) operates throughout. ⟨ф ц щ⟩ occur mainly in Russian loanwords. ⟨ъ⟩ marks a glottal stop /ʔ/ in native words (e.g. before a stem-initial vowel) and is kept as its own grapheme; ⟨ь⟩ marks palatalisation of the preceding consonant rather than an independent segment and is omitted from the grapheme map. ⟨дж⟩ /dʒ/ is kept as its own grapheme key (not derived from ⟨д⟩ /d/ + ⟨ж⟩ /ʒ/) because it spells a single post-alveolar affricate phoneme, the same segment written with a dedicated single letter in the closely related South Siberian Turkic Cyrillic alphabets (cf. Khakas ⟨ӌ⟩, Shor ⟨ҷ⟩); Kumyk's 1938 alphabet reused the two-letter Russian digraph convention for this phoneme instead of minting a new letter.
